subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Which lifecycle hook contract should OpenClaw expose for subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call thresholds: workspace/internal hooks, typed plugin hooks, or a split contract by sensitivity?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the decision affects public API naming, hook authority, raw result/session exposure, mid-turn execution, and new configuration semantics, so automation should not lock in the product or security boundary.

options.title: Design One Split-Surface Contract
options.body: Define the internal/workspace observation events and typed plugin runtime-control events together, with payload and security rules before implementation.

options.title: Observation-Only First
options.body: Land only coarse non-mutating completion and turn observation events now, then decide mid-turn thresholds and mutation separately.

options.title: Typed Plugin Hooks Only
options.body: Keep sensitive lifecycle data and mid-turn behavior out of workspace hooks and expose them only through the plugin SDK with explicit trust gates.

recommendation.title: Design One Split-Surface Contract
recommendation.body: Define the internal/workspace observation events and typed plugin runtime-control events together, with payload and security rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` has the strongest combined signal from hook docs/source history and current product/API direction for core-vs-plugin extension boundaries.
